blocks.orig: After you’ve booked one of our Tanzania safaris or Zanzibar holidays (hooray!), the next thing is to apply for your tourist visa. For many, this leads to worries and insecurities. How to apply? Where to apply? What documents do I need? Luckily for you, getting a visa for Tanzania is relatively easy, especially when booking with us. Read on to know more.
blocks.html: Once you have booked one of our safaris in Tanzania or holidays on Zanzibar (great news!), your next step is applying for a tourist visa. Many people find this worrying and feel unsure about it. How do you apply? Where? Which documents are required? Fortunately, a Tanzanian visa is fairly simple to arrange, particularly if you book with us. Keep reading to find out more.

blocks.orig: When travelling to Tanzania, you can either get your visa online or upon arrival*. Both ways are fine and valid, even though the Tanzanian government prefers you use the online option, as they are keen to show Tanzania is a modern country. Below, we broke down more pros and cons of both ways of applying. But first, let’s talk about the costs.
blocks.html: For a trip to Tanzania you can obtain your visa either online or on arrival*. Both options are valid and acceptable, although the government of Tanzania would rather you applied online, because it wants to present Tanzania as a modern country. Further down we have set out the advantages and disadvantages of each route. Let's start with the costs, though.

blocks.orig: The costs for a Tanzania visa differ slightly per nationality. Are you coming from Europe? Then the fee is 50 USD. Are you a US citizen? Then you need a multi-entry visa for the price of 100 USD. Both are valid for three months, but the multi-entry visa allows you to leave the country and come back again with the same visa within one year.
blocks.html: What you pay for a Tanzanian visa varies a little depending on your nationality. Travelling from Europe? Then you pay 50 USD. If you hold US citizenship, you need a multi-entry visa, which costs 100 USD. Each is valid for three months, but with the multi-entry visa you can leave Tanzania and return on the same visa within a year.

blocks.orig: The amounts above apply when you purchase your visa online. If you apply upon arrival, the costs are either 50 USD or 50 EUR (or 100 USD for the multi-entry visa). A bit surprising because, of course, 50 EUR is worth more than 50 USD. In any case, you can also pay with a credit card, and then the fee is 50 or 100 USD plus credit card fees. It’s up to you.
blocks.html: These prices are for visas bought online. On arrival, the fee is 50 USD or 50 EUR (or 100 USD for a multi-entry visa). That is slightly odd, since 50 EUR is obviously worth more than 50 USD. You can also pay by credit card, in which case you pay 50 or 100 USD plus the card charges. It’s your choice.

blocks.orig: The Tanzanian government prefers it when you apply online, and truth be told, it does have its perks:
blocks.html: Applying online is what the Tanzanian government would like you to do, and to be honest, there are some real advantages:

blocks.orig: The process is relatively easy, especially with the explanatory PDF you get when booking through us.
blocks.html: It is a fairly straightforward process, all the more so with the explanatory PDF we send you when you book with us.

blocks.orig: You board your plane knowing your visa is arranged and paid for.
blocks.html: When you get on the plane, you know your visa has been sorted and paid.

blocks.orig: Upon arrival, you only have to wait at one counter to get your visa stamped.
blocks.html: After landing, you only need to wait at a single counter for your visa stamp.

blocks.orig: To apply for a visa online, you go to the official portal of the Tanzanian government. We advise you to NOT apply through any other website because they are either more expensive or scams. We know of several travellers who lost their money through these scams, so it’s better to be safe than sorry. The official portal is:
blocks.html: An online application is made through the official portal of the government of Tanzania. Please do NOT use any other website, as these are either pricier or fraudulent. We know a number of travellers who lost money to such scams, so it pays to be careful. You will find the official portal here:

blocks.orig: People booking with us get a special PDF to guide them through the process. And our travel consultants are always available for advice. We cannot apply for your visa for you, but this way, you can hardly go wrong. After submitting your application, it can take up to ten days before your visa is processed and approved. Make sure to take a print or download it with you when you go. Upon arrival, you only have to queue at the immigration counter to get your visa stamped in your passport. Then you collect your bags, and you’re good to go.
blocks.html: If you book with us, you receive a special PDF that walks you through each step, and our travel consultants are always on hand to advise you. We are not able to submit the visa application on your behalf, but with this help it is hard to make a mistake. Once you have sent your application, processing and approval can take as long as ten days. Be sure to bring a printed copy or a download of it on your trip. When you land, you simply join the queue at the immigration counter to have the visa stamped into your passport. After that you pick up your luggage and you are ready to go.

blocks.orig: APPLY FOR A VISA UPON ARRIVAL IN TANZANIA
blocks.html: GETTING YOUR VISA ON ARRIVAL IN TANZANIA

blocks.orig: If you cannot or do not want to apply online, people from most countries* can also apply upon arrival (as of January 2026). Brace yourself for some nice African bureaucracy, but other than that, the process is quite easy:
blocks.html: Can't or don't want to apply online? Then, as of January 2026, travellers from most countries* can also get their visa on arrival. Be ready for a little African bureaucracy; apart from that, it is a fairly simple procedure:

blocks.orig: You fill out an application form upon arrival at the airport (keep a pen at hand and have the address of Your Tanzania Trip and your first lodge at the ready).
blocks.html: When you land at the airport, you complete an application form (have a pen with you and keep the address of Your Tanzania Trip and of your first lodge handy).

blocks.orig: Go to a second counter to pay your visa fee, and pay either in cash or by credit card.
blocks.html: Then head to a second counter to pay the visa fee, in cash or by credit card.

blocks.orig: Go to a third counter and get the visa stamped in your passport.
blocks.html: At a third counter, your passport receives the visa stamp.

blocks.orig: As you can see, when applying upon arrival, you have to queue three times, whereas if you apply online, you only queue once upon arrival. So applying the old-fashioned way might slow you down a bit, but hey, you are in the country of ‘pole pole’ now – no hurry in Africa! You might as well get used to it. And just between you and us: these days, most people apply online, so the one queue for online applications is way longer than the three queues you take when applying upon arrival. Heck, you might even be out quicker!
blocks.html: So with a visa on arrival you stand in line three times, while an online application means just one queue when you land. The traditional route may hold you up a little, but remember, you are now in the land of ‘pole pole’ – there's no rush in Africa! Better get used to it straight away. And between ourselves: as most travellers now apply online, the single queue for online visas is often far longer than the three queues for visas on arrival. You may even get through faster!

blocks.orig: Nowadays, most people prefer to apply online, just to be sure to have that visa in their pocket before travelling. Which is understandable. If you decide to apply online, make sure to be prepared:
blocks.html: These days most travellers choose to apply online, simply so they know they have the visa in hand before they leave. That makes sense. If you go for the online option, be well prepared:

blocks.orig: Apply three to four weeks before travelling, in case your application gets denied. This will give you enough time to correct the mistakes and apply again.
blocks.html: Submit your application three to four weeks before your trip, in case it is rejected. That leaves you time to fix any errors and reapply.

blocks.orig: Have a credit card ready for your payment, or know how to make an international bank transfer.
blocks.html: Keep a credit card at hand to pay, or make sure you know how to send an international bank transfer.

blocks.orig: Have a digital passport-size picture, a picture of your passport’s biodata page (max 300 kB) and a PDF of your flight ticket (max 1 MB) ready.
blocks.html: Prepare a digital passport photo, a photo of the biodata page of your passport (max 300 kB) and a PDF of your plane ticket (max 1 MB).

blocks.orig: Make sure your passport is valid for six months upon return from Tanzania.
blocks.html: Check that your passport will still be valid for six months after you return from Tanzania.

blocks.orig: If children travel with only one parent, you need a written document in English with the consent of the other parent for the trip, and then you have to upload this into the system.
blocks.html: When children are travelling with just one parent, you need a written letter in English in which the other parent consents to the trip, which you then upload into the system.

blocks.orig: Make sure to have a pen at hand when arriving in Tanzania, because sometimes there is still a form they ask you to fill.
blocks.html: Bring a pen for your arrival in Tanzania, as you are sometimes still asked to complete a form.

blocks.orig: If you decide to be a bit adventurous and apply upon arrival, don’t board the plane unprepared either.
blocks.html: Feeling a little adventurous and planning to get your visa on arrival? Then make sure you are prepared before you fly as well.

blocks.orig: Carry the amount needed for the fee in cash (USD/EUR), or use your credit card.
blocks.html: Bring the fee in cash (USD/EUR), or pay with your credit card.

blocks.orig: Have a pen at hand to fill in the application form, and the addresses of Your Tanzania Trip and the first hotel you stay in.
blocks.html: Keep a pen ready for the application form, along with the addresses of Your Tanzania Trip and of your first hotel.

blocks.orig: If children travel with only one parent, you need a written document in English with the consent of the other parent for the trip.
blocks.html: When children are travelling with just one parent, you need a written letter in English in which the other parent consents to the trip.

blocks.orig: It’s up to you how you apply for your visa – whatever gives you the least stress. As long as you keep the end goal in mind: to get that visa. Because only with your visa in hand can you get your bags and start your safari adventure with us.
blocks.html: How you apply for your visa is entirely your choice – go with whatever feels least stressful. Just keep the aim in sight: getting the visa. Only once you have it can you collect your luggage and begin your safari adventure with us.

blocks.orig: *Nationals of some countries need a so-called Referral Visa and are not allowed to apply upon arrival. So make sure to check that before you decide how to apply. Also, applying upon arrival might not be possible anymore in the future for anyone, so make sure to check the immigration guidelines before you leave to confirm that it’s still possible.
blocks.html: *Citizens of certain countries require a Referral Visa and cannot apply on arrival. Please check this before choosing how to apply. Visas on arrival may also be discontinued for everyone at some point, so before you travel, look at the immigration guidelines to make sure the option still exists.
